title: openai-wire-probes-report-to-the-watch
intention: Every standing WATCHME probe berthed in cairn/machines/openai_wire reports to harbor_master's watch verb with {ticket, holds, finding} stated against its own ticket's falsifier, and each spec names that receiver.
why: Every standing probe in cairn/machines/openai_wire mails with no verb and nothing uses it (835b5736bf2b D2); a88d6a368cfb built the watch verb that uses a WATCHME finding and 8ecb99998254 built watch_carry. Akien's answer to open-291189a9766a: build the receivers.
traces_to: 835b5736bf2b's falsifier (zero probe-bearing standing specs lack a receiver) and Akien's answer to open-291189a9766a; the 2026-09-30 ruling that a probe's data must have a consumer that USES it; RULE 1 (the build stays inside cairn/machines/openai_wire; base's helper through its public interface, harbor_master through its bus verb)
how: Measured 2026-10-03: 1 tickets at a rest carry a watchme probe under cairn/machines/openai_wire/probes/ (76639374d9f9). Read 2026-10-03: one standing ticket (76639374d9f9, at PROVED) carries a probe under cairn/machines/openai_wire/probes, posting to='harbor_master' with no verb. Its trigger is distinct >= 1 holder of the machine and its enough is distinct >= 2; 'one holder forever is the finding' is stated in the spec's enough, and the probe declares _HORIZON = 1000 pulses, past which BaseShim.overdue surfaces it. One proof imports it: cairn/machines/openai_wire/proofs/test_probe.py (asserts fires/gathered_enough, payload carries 'ticket' and 'against_falsifier', PROBE.to == 'harbor_master' and horizon == 1000; never the verb). Each PROBE gets verb='watch' and carry=watch_carry(<its id>, _carry, <its predicate>), importing watch_carry from cairn.tools.base.probe (declared public). Each ticket's watchme spec gains receiver {what: 'harbor_master watch verb', in: 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'} through the artifact door. A proof under cairn/machines/openai_wire/proofs reads the population from the commons and asserts each probe's verb, to, and live payload invariants.
falsifier: GREEN when every ticket at PROVED or WATCHME whose watchme.probe sits under cairn/machines/openai_wire has a probe whose PROBE posts verb 'watch' to 'harbor_master' and whose payload over live data carries ticket == that ticket's id, holds a bool, and a non-empty finding whenever holds is False; and every such spec names receiver {what: 'harbor_master watch verb', in: 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'} with watchme_spec_error naming no receiver fault. RED if any standing openai_wire spec lacks the receiver, or if a converted payload's ticket is a path or another id. WRONG INTENT if a openai_wire probe's data has a reader other than its own ticket's FIXME that only Akien could name.
watchme: none, because what this child's probes say is read by harbor_master's watch verb (a88d6a368cfb, PROVED), and whether they ever fire is 164da559823d's and acb4ecd84364's watch (CairnCommons/tickets/164da559823d-*.json); a probe on probes reporting would need a receiver of its own.
children: none, because the change is 1 PROBE declarations and their specs, all inside cairn/machines/openai_wire.

Its trigger is count-shaped (TRUE from the first holder on) and its enough is TWO holders, so a post is a progress report, never a fault: it gains this holds predicate, inserted exactly as follows just above PROBE = Probe(: def _holds(context: dict) -> bool: ⏎     """One holder is the watch still counting toward TWO, not a fault: the trigger fires from the ⏎     first holder so the count means something, and "one holder forever" is a finding only the ⏎     horizon can name (BaseShim.overdue at _HORIZON pulses), never a single post. A survey that ⏎     raises reads as holds False through watch_carry (835b5736bf2b child).""" ⏎     return True ; and passes carry=watch_carry(_TICKET_ID, _carry, holds=_holds). This follows engine_trace_corpus (4b2338feed4d, under 3c035a838446), whose growth report is likewise holds True. Nothing else in a probe changes. decisions.text: D1: the probes — In each of these files under cairn/machines/openai_wire/probes/: openai_wire_is_included_by_a_second_holder.py (76639374d9f9: constant _TICKET_ID — add it; holds=_holds) — append watch_carry to the existing `from cairn.tools.base.probe import ...` line; where the constant is to be added, add `<constant> = "<its id>"` after the import block; in `PROBE = Probe(...)` replace `carry=_carry,` with `verb="watch",` and `carry=watch_carry(<constant>, _carry, <its predicate>),`. openai_wire_is_included_by_a_second_holder holds _OWNING_TICKET as a slug ('openai-wire-is-a-machine-anybody-can-include'); that constant stays and a new _TICKET_ID carries 76639374d9f9. Its trigger is count-shaped (TRUE from the first holder on) and its enough is TWO holders, so a post is a progress report, never a fault: it gains this holds predicate, inserted exactly as follows just above PROBE = Probe(: def _holds(context: dict) -> bool: ⏎     """One holder is the watch still counting toward TWO, not a fault: the trigger fires from the ⏎     first holder so the count means something, and "one holder forever" is a finding only the ⏎     horizon can name (BaseShim.overdue at _HORIZON pulses), never a single post. A survey that ⏎     raises reads as holds False through watch_carry (835b5736bf2b child).""" ⏎     return True ; and passes carry=watch_carry(_TICKET_ID, _carry, holds=_holds). This follows engine_trace_corpus (4b2338feed4d, under 3c035a838446), whose growth report is likewise holds True. watch_carry's signature (cairn/tools/base/probe.py): watch_carry(ticket_id: str, carry=None, *, fails=None, holds=None), exactly one of fails=/holds= given as a keyword. <its predicate> is the literal keyword argument named in the parentheses above for that file: `fails=_trigger` passes the probe's existing module-level `_trigger` function (the same one already given to Probe as trigger=), and needs no new function. `holds=_holds` passes a `_holds` function defined as stated in this decision. Each named file exists (read 2026-10-03) with a `from cairn.tools.base.probe import ...` line and a `PROBE = Probe(...)` call holding `carry=_carry,`. Nothing else changes; watch_carry is not edited.

D2: the proof — Create cairn/machines/openai_wire/proofs/test_openai_wire_probes_report_to_the_watch.py by copying the existing file cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_probes_report_to_the_watch.py (sealed green under 8d3c36e1fe59) byte for byte and then making ONLY these modifications: with the docstring naming cairn/machines/openai_wire and ticket 4c18deb605f6; PROVES = {'4c18deb605f6': {'all': 'test_openai_wire_probes_report_to_the_watch'}}; BERTH = 'cairn/machines/openai_wire/probes/'; _REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4] (the repo root: the directory holding cairn/); teeth renamed test_every_standing_openai_wire_probe_posts_watch, test_every_standing_openai_wire_spec_names_the_receiver and the composite test_openai_wire_probes_report_to_the_watch. Structure, in full: imports importlib, json, subprocess, sys, Path; _REPO_ROOT on sys.path; parse_workflow from cairn.tools.base.transitions; watchme_spec_error from cairn.tools.base.watchme_spec; _main_tree() = Path(git -C _REPO_ROOT rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir).parent falling back to _REPO_ROOT; _tickets() = _main_tree().parent/'CairnCommons'/'tickets'; _standing() = (id, doc, spec) for each ticket whose parse_workflow(doc['workflow_and_state']).here is 'PROVED' or 'WATCHME' (a ticket that does not parse is skipped) whose watchme spec's probe starts with BERTH (every such spec: a ticket whose watchme is a list may contribute more than one tuple, and _specs() reads a dict or a list of dicts), asserting non-empty with `assert out, ...`; the posts tooth imports each probe module, takes payload = PROBE.payload({}) (Probe.payload runs the carry over that context), and asserts PROBE.verb == 'watch', PROBE.to == 'harbor_master', payload({}) carries ticket == the id, holds a bool, non-empty finding when holds is False (invariants only); the receiver tooth asserts spec['receiver'] == {'what': 'harbor_master watch verb', 'in': 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'} and watchme_spec_error(doc) names no receiver fault; a __main__ block runs each, prints PASS/FAIL, exits 1 on any failure. No classes.

D3: the specs' receiver — Write one Python script file (in the session scratchpad) that does the following, and run it. Ticket files are /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/tickets/<id>-<slug>.json (glob '<id>-*.json', exactly one). For each of 76639374d9f9: doc = json.loads(Path(p).read_text()); the watchme is a dict or list of dicts; every spec whose 'probe' starts with 'cairn/machines/openai_wire/probes/' (one or several) gets spec['receiver'] = {'what': 'harbor_master watch verb', 'in': 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'}; then cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write(p, json.dumps(doc, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n', verb='cast', why='<id>: the watchme names its receiver, harbor_master\'s watch verb (4c18deb605f6)') — write(path, text, *, verb, why), text the WHOLE modified ticket. Run it as a script file (a shell command naming a record path and writing is refused by the artifact gate).

D4: green, seal, commit — Run cairn/machines/openai_wire/proofs/test_openai_wire_probes_report_to_the_watch.py (exit 0) and the probe-importing proofs (cairn/machines/openai_wire/proofs/test_probe.py); each must be green. Seal with `bin/cairn test --seal --timeout 900 cairn/machines/openai_wire/proofs/test_openai_wire_probes_report_to_the_watch.py <the probe-importing proofs>` (it runs each and writes its validation beside it). Commit with message '4c18deb605f6: openai_wire probes report to the watch' (the commit runs the reseal ladder, so allow an hour); commit the commons.

The proof is created by copying the existing file cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_probes_report_to_the_watch.py byte for byte (cp), then making ONLY the modifications this ticket lists (docstring, PROVES, BERTH, _REPO_ROOT depth, the three tooth names, plus any tooth this ticket adds). No generator script exists or is used: any earlier mention of child.py names a scratch script of the caster, not something the builder runs. The posts tooth obtains each payload as PROBE.payload({}) — Probe.payload runs the carry over that context.

The receiver is set by ONE Python script file the builder writes in the session scratchpad and runs: for each ticket id it globs the one ticket file, json-loads it, sets spec["receiver"] on every watchme spec whose probe starts with the berth path, and calls cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write(path, json.dumps(doc, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", verb="cast", why=...). A shell command naming a record path while writing is refused by the artifact gate, which is why it is a script file.

watch_carry is defined in cairn/tools/base/probe.py as watch_carry(ticket_id: str, carry=None, *, fails=None, holds=None) — exactly one of fails=/holds= passed as a keyword. "<its predicate>" is the literal keyword argument named for each file in this decision: fails=_trigger passes that probe module's existing module-level _trigger function (the one already given to Probe(trigger=...)); holds=_holds passes the _holds function this decision says to add. Example: carry=watch_carry(_TICKET_ID, _carry, fails=_trigger).
